subject: Post-call: multilingual quality checks + proposed eval plan

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: multilingual quality checks + proposed eval plan

Hi Anna (and Kenji),

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same view: 

- Goal: evaluate model options for multilingual customer support summarization and intent extraction across German, Swedish, Japanese.
- Constraints: low latency requirement for EU region (200–400ms p95), strict PII removal in pipeline, and limited budget for initial pilot.

Immediate asks from Redwood:
1) Permission to run a short offline eval on the sample prompt set you shared (we attached a cleaned prompt set).
2) Confirmation of the target languages: DE, SV, JA (Anna — you mentioned NL/CZ could be Phase 2).
3) Benchmarks you care about: ROUGE/L, exact-match for extraction labels, and human-quality checks for fluency/appropriateness.

What we propose for the PoC (high-level):
- Run parallel evals on 3 candidate variants: a 13B quantized variant optimized for latency, a mid-size ~6B low-latency model, and a conservative large-context model for high-quality summarization.
- Produce per-language precision/recall and a short human-review matrix (3 native reviewers per language).
- Deliver a short report and recommended canary config + estimated token cost.

Attachments: prompt-set-eu-apac-v1.csv (sample prompts)
Related links: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3C-redwood-benchmarks

Next steps: if you confirm the list of languages and sign-off to run the evals, we’ll kick off by Monday and share preliminary numbers within 48–72 hours.

Cheers,
Sergio

On Thu, 11 Jun 2026 at 09:00, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marissa / Priyom — forwarding the thread and the prompt set Anna approved. Please treat this as a high-priority PoC request. Key asks:

Quick status + preliminary findings (first 48h run):

What we ran:
- Candidate models: redwood-open-13b-q4_16k (latency-optimized q4), redwood-mid-6b-int8, and rwdx-35b-std (high quality).
- Inputs: prompt-set-eu-apac-v1.csv (DE/SV/JA) + small internal baseline containing prior DE support tickets.

Automated metrics (high level):
- DE: 13B-q4 achieves best latency (p95 ~220ms) with ROUGE/L ~0.68; extraction EM 0.74. High-qual rwdx-35b has better ROUGE/L (0.74) but p95 ~680ms.
- SV: mid-6b-int8 performs well on extraction EM (0.71) and is fastest; human fluency scores (n=3) avg 4.2/5.
- JA: rwdx-35b gives best fluency/adequacy, but hallucination risk around SKU normalization seen on 13B-q4.

Regression notes / failure modes we observed:
- Entity truncation on long DE product descriptions when sequence length cap hit — mitigated by dynamic KV caching but needs config tweaks.
- Price/date formatting: models default to US formatting in several DE/SV outputs — prompt-level formatting constraints help but we should add locale post-processing for strict compliance.
- JA: polite form (keigo) variance — we recommend a lightweight post-processing normalization or a small prompt-template enforcing style.

Attachments uploaded: redwood-multilang-benchmarks-20260611.pdf (detailed per-language tables), prompt-set-eu-apac-v1.csv (outputs.csv included in drive link).
Related links: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/evals/multilang-eu-apac-2026

Recommendation for PoC canary: start with redwood-open-13b-q4_16k in EU region with a small canary fleet (3 GPUs), enable prefix caching and a prompt-level locale constraint, and route spellout/format normalization to a lightweight postprocessor. For JA, run the rwdx-35b as a validation variant for higher-value messages only.

Next steps:
- Sergio: confirm budget envelope for the pilot so I can size the canary.
- Anna / Kenji: confirm acceptance criteria for human-quality (we used 3 native reviewers, threshold avg >= 4/5).

— Marissa
